name: Fictional ColdLoop Container Rental
industry_detail: Reusable takeaway containers and reverse logistics
problem: Independent restaurants discard single-use takeaway containers. Returning reusable containers is inconvenient for their customers.
solution: Rent a pool of reusable takeaway containers to restaurants and collect, wash and redistribute returned containers.
intended_customers: Restaurant owner-managers are buyers; takeaway diners return the containers. Start with independent lunch restaurants in one compact district.
budget: SAR 50000 total available startup budget; this is not a sales forecast.
business_model: B2B rental service. Own the container pool and organise collection and washing through a partner. Restaurant staff handle issue and return records.
value_proposition: Reduce restaurant packaging waste without asking each restaurant to operate its own washing and collection service.
revenue_model: Proposed monthly restaurant subscription of SAR 800 for a shared container pool. This price has not been tested; replacement/deposit terms are undecided.
market_opportunity: Fictional demonstration input: three restaurant managers expressed informal interest, with no signed orders or willingness-to-pay evidence. No market-size study is available.
competition: Alternatives identified in the plan are disposable containers and restaurants operating their own reusable containers. No named competitor research has been performed.
cost_structure: Washing partner price, collection costs, container purchase cost, container loss rate and staff costs are not yet known.
growth_strategy: Pilot with two nearby restaurants before considering more collection districts. Measure actual returns and collection effort.
current_challenges: No washing partner agreement; container hygiene process, diner return incentives and lost-container responsibility remain unresolved.

name: Fictional ClinicRoster Scheduling SaaS
industry_detail: Appointment scheduling software for physiotherapy clinics
problem: Small physiotherapy clinics double-book rooms when several receptionists update paper diaries.
solution: A cloud scheduling tool with receptionist access controls, conflict detection and room calendars. The first version will use fictional appointment records for testing.
intended_customers: Independent physiotherapy clinic owners pay; receptionists schedule appointments and therapists view room availability.
business_model: B2B software subscription; the founder contracts development and supports clinic onboarding.
value_proposition: Prevent room-booking conflicts with a lightweight workflow instead of requiring a clinic to replace its entire management system.
revenue_model: Proposed SAR 450 per clinic per month. The founder assumes 100 paying clinics in the first month but has no sales pipeline or signed customers.
market_opportunity: Fictional demonstration input: six clinic administrators were interviewed informally, three of whom preferred keeping paper diaries. No verified market-size data is available.
competition: Owner-identified alternatives: paper diaries, shared spreadsheets and existing clinic-management software. No named competitor or pricing research is supplied.
cost_structure: An unverified development quote of SAR 45000 and an estimated SAR 800 monthly hosting budget are supplied. Support, security review, onboarding, messaging and maintenance costs are not specified.
growth_strategy: Pilot with three clinics in Jeddah, train receptionists and measure booking conflicts before expanding. Pricing and retention have not been tested.
current_challenges: Founder lacks a technical cofounder; data-access permissions, reliability, backups and clinic integrations are unresolved.
